newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam trade gap sparks calls for import control.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam trade gap sparks calls for import control.

text.p: Vietnam's Government Statistics Office said on Wednesday that the country's economy was at risk from a fast growing trade deficit and warned that measures were needed to tackle the problem, including restrictions on imports.
The office issued data showing the gap between imports and exports widened to a record $3.537 billion between January 1 and September 10.
By comparison, the total trade deficit for all of 1995 was $2.3 billion.
The office said in a statement that the deficit was not yet having a major impact on the economy, but added that it was "much higher than should be allowed."
It called for increased measures to tackle smuggling, and said restrictions should be imposed on the import of foreign products such as cement, which are already made in Vietnam.
The statement said a prime factor behind the gap was imports of machinery and material for new industry, especially in the foreign-invested sector.
It said imports for this sector accounted for 22.2 percent of the total deficit.
Vietnamese and foreign economists have expressed concern over the trade imbalance, which has become a blotch on an otherwise healthy economic outlook.
However, the statistics department said it was not too late to address the problem.
"The socio-economic situation in the past nine months has followed a generally positive trend," it said.
"If from now until the end of the year we have suitable resolutions, then export value will exceed the target of $6.6 billion and the deficit will be reduced to around $3.0 billion," it said.
